channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: This Week in Source Control: 18 November 2026
item.description: This roundup covers the latest updates in version control software, including significant release notes for Gerrit 3.15.0 and GitButler 0.23.4. It also highlights security disclosures, specifically regarding multiple CVEs patched in Gitea 28.4.0.

item.title: Are vibe-coded games making me a substance dualist?
item.description: The author explores the unsettling feeling of 'soullessness' in AI-generated, vibe-coded video games, contrasting technical explanations with an intuitive sense of human presence. While some issues can be attributed to design flaws, the author questions whether our perception of art involves an intangible quality that transcends rational analysis.

item.title: Supersequences and Superpermutations
item.description: This article explores the mathematical concepts of supersequences and superpermutations, focusing on how universal words contain every permutation of an alphabet as a subsequence. It highlights the distinction between subsequence-based universal words and contiguous substring arrangements.

item.title: In the Microsoft employee price list, why did the BASIC compiler cost less than the BASIC interpreter?
item.description: This post explores the historical pricing strategy behind early Microsoft software products. It examines why the BASIC compiler was priced lower than the BASIC interpreter in internal employee price lists.

item.title: "No way to prevent this" say users of only language where this regularly happens
item.description: This article serves as a satirical commentary on software engineering pain points, specifically focusing on the common frustrations developers face when dealing with poorly designed programming languages. It highlights the irony of recurring technical issues that developers are forced to endure despite their predictable nature.

item.title: Once More Unto The Breach - Another Year In Review
item.description: The author reflects on their second year of FIRE (Financial Independence, Retire Early) after leaving their job in 2010. They share personal experiences of a relaxed lifestyle, including travel, entertainment, and social engagements, while evaluating their post-retirement journey.

item.title: Pluralistic: Enshittifiers groom us for scammers (18 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that the current 'enshittification' of corporate and digital services creates an environment where scams become indistinguishable from standard business practices. The integration of AI tools further empowers fraudsters to conduct large-scale, personalized attacks, eroding trust in public institutions and digital security.

item.title: Quoting Daniel Stenberg
item.description: Daniel Stenberg challenges the effectiveness of automated AI code migration tools by comparing them to the active maintenance of the curl project. He argues that automated rewrites fail to keep pace with the continuous bug fixes and security improvements made by human maintainers.

item.title: The PSF end-of-year fundraiser
item.description: Simon Willison highlights the Python Software Foundation's end-of-year fundraiser, which supports essential operations like PyPI, community events, and the Developers in Residence program. He encourages individuals and companies that benefit from Python to contribute to the non-profit's mission.

item.title: I joined the NTP Pool, but not with my Stratum 1 Pi
item.description: Jeff Geerling explains his recent contribution to the NTP Pool by setting up a public Stratum 2 time server. The server derives its time from his local Stratum 1 hardware, which utilizes a Raspberry Pi connected to a high-precision u-blox ZED-F9T GNSS module.

item.title: Beyond Linux: A Journey Through the Open Source Ecosystem
item.description: This blog post explores the open source ecosystem beyond Linux, discussing alternative operating systems like BSD and illumos. The author shares his personal journey of discovering free software and reflects on the broader philosophy of knowledge sharing and technical freedom.

item.title: My Empire of Sunshine and Roses
item.description: The author explores the nature of historical impact through counterfactual thinking and the challenge of individual agency in a seemingly deterministic world. They examine the trajectory of AI development, questioning whether current industry models like centralized offices or expensive agent swarms are truly sustainable or effective.

item.title: Stacked diffs with Maiao
item.description: The article discusses the benefits of using Maiao, a tool designed to simplify the workflow for developers who prefer stacked diffs when working on traditional platforms like GitHub. It explains the concept of pull requests and branches, positioning Maiao as an effective solution for managing code reviews more efficiently.

item.title: How can I ask a second program to show a dialog box as if it were shown by my first program?
item.description: The article explains that there is no native system mechanism to force one program to display a dialog box as if it originated from another. To achieve this, developers must manually coordinate window management between the two applications.

item.title: HomeAssistant - shrink a HAOS qcow2 filesystem
item.description: This guide details the process of shrinking a HomeAssistant OS (HAOS) qcow2 virtual disk to reclaim unused storage space. It provides technical steps to resolve the discrepancy between the actual filesystem usage and the virtual disk's allocated size.

item.title: Pluralistic: Remembrance of proteins past (17 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This post highlights Scott Colom's historic and successful Mississippi senate campaign, specifically praising his highly effective political advertisement. It also serves as a daily link digest covering various topics including DRM, corporate practices, and current political discourse.

item.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
item.description: Attackers exploited a security vulnerability in the Optimizely platform to inject malware into at least 178 major websites, including high-profile destinations like the BBC and CNN. The incident highlights significant risks posed by third-party content providers and the lack of strict security enforcement for external scripts on popular web platforms.

item.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
item.description: Simon Willison introduces the 'external sandbox' pattern for AI coding agents to execute code safely outside the host machine. The post provides three reference implementations using different technologies like WebAssembly, Apple Containers, and Quicksand to isolate agent-driven code execution.

item.title: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol
item.description: Simon Willison details the release of OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol models, highlighting their API availability and pricing adjustments. The post provides benchmarks through 'pelican' image generation tests to compare the performance and improvements over previous model iterations.

item.title: Running the full server-side Datasette Python app in the browser with service workers and Pyodide
item.description: Simon Willison has updated Datasette Lite, a browser-based port of the Datasette application using Pyodide and service workers. This tool allows users to run complex SQLite data analysis and install plugins directly in the browser via custom URLs, eliminating the need for a dedicated server.

item.title: Quoting Go Proverbs
item.description: This post highlights a key maxim from the Go Proverbs, emphasizing that minimal code duplication is often preferable to excessive software dependencies. It reflects on the importance of balancing code simplicity against modularity in programming.

item.title: Weekly Update 530: Email Dependencies & Apps
item.description: This update explores the critical reliance on email as a fundamental utility, similar to water or power. It highlights the potential risks and cascading failures that occur when email service providers face unexpected downtime.

item.title: My Empire of Dirt
item.description: The author critiques the 'Singleton' ideology held by AI development leaders, arguing that their pursuit of autonomous, self-generating agent systems will lead to societal exclusion and geopolitical conflict. The post suggests that these developments will likely trigger a third world war rather than human extinction, with a pessimistic outlook on current strategic and resource-based outcomes.

item.title: Paul Christiano – We could be 12 months away from AIs that can overthrow the government
item.description: AI researcher Paul Christiano warns that humanity could be only 12 months away from developing AI systems capable of overthrowing governments. The discussion emphasizes the potential existential risks and the difficulty of recovery if such powerful systems are misaligned.

item.title: Here's how anyone can easily use private, open weight models
item.description: This article explores the utility of Large Language Models while addressing privacy concerns regarding centralized providers like OpenAI. It argues that users can leverage powerful AI tools independently by utilizing private, open-weight models.

item.title: Taxis and hash functions
item.description: This article highlights a real-world security failure where NYC taxi data was anonymized using the insecure MD5 hash function. It explains why MD5 is vulnerable to brute-force attacks and illustrates the risks of relying on flawed cryptographic practices for privacy protection.

item.title: Orbital footnote
item.description: This post discusses the orbital characteristics of the dwarf planet candidate ED138. The author demonstrates how Kepler's third law can be used to derive orbital information from basic astronomical data.

item.title: Gig Review: ABBA Voyage ★★★★☆
item.description: The author reflects on a visit to the ABBA museum in Stockholm, highlighting the group's massive cultural influence despite his initial lack of fandom. The piece specifically touches on the exhibition detailing the innovative 'Voyage' concert experience in London.

item.title: llm 0.37.3
item.description: Simon Willison released LLM 0.37.3, a bug fix update addressing compatibility issues with SQLite 3.54.1. The release resolves a regression where JSON handling in SQL queries was altered, requiring a code workaround to ensure proper data formatting.

item.title: What’s Next For Nvidia?
item.description: Steve Blank examines the potential future of Nvidia following the announcement of Jensen Huang's resignation. The article explores the systemic risks that companies face when a visionary leader departs, highlighting the common decline in innovation and momentum.

item.title: ASI as a Black Box
item.description: This article explores the inherent uncertainty surrounding Artificial Superintelligence (ASI), characterizing it as a 'black box.' The author argues that current predictions fail to capture the true nature of superintelligence because we lack any empirical understanding of what it would actually entail.

item.title: Taking AI Seriously
item.description: This article explores the philosophical and practical implications of treating artificial intelligence as a significant, transformative force. It examines the necessity of shifting our perspective on AI from novelty to a critical infrastructure component.

item.title: Variable Electricity Pricing - the Highs and the Lows
item.description: The author shares their experience using a variable electricity pricing tariff with a smart meter, which allows for dynamic half-hourly rates. They highlight the financial benefits of the system, including instances where energy prices become negative, effectively paying the user to consume power.

item.title: People will lose their jobs over GTA 6
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author shares a personal anecdote about prioritizing the release of Metal Gear Solid 5 over client maintenance work. The story highlights the tension between professional responsibilities and the intense cultural anticipation surrounding major video game launches like GTA 6.

item.title: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released datasette-maplibre 0.1a0, a new geospatial plugin for Datasette that integrates MapLibre GL with OpenFreeMap. Developed with AI assistance, the plugin features lazy-loading WebGL previews and a comprehensive demo available via Datasette Lite.

item.title: datasette 1.0a43
item.description: Datasette 1.0a43 introduces streaming support for output renderers and various UI improvements, including a new web component and JSON formatting. This release also addresses critical security vulnerabilities regarding private stored queries and incorporates several community contributions.

item.title: datasette 0.65.6
item.description: Datasette version 0.65.6 has been released, incorporating a critical security backport. The update fixes a vulnerability where unauthorized users could download databases with mismatched route and name parameters.

item.title: datasette-apps 0.4a0
item.description: Datasette Apps 0.4a0 introduces support for URL fragment linking, enabling sandboxed applications to communicate and reference each other. This update allows for modular app design where separate tools can effectively search and link to specific data records.

item.title: datasette-agent 0.6a0
item.description: Datasette Agent version 0.6a0 has been released, introducing several bug fixes and a new agent prompt feature on the Datasette homepage. Users can now interact with their data more intuitively by using hash-mentions to reference tables and queries directly within the input field.

item.title: Of Course People Hate Data Centres
item.description: This article explores the growing public opposition to data center construction, highlighting statistics that show widespread disapproval across political lines in the US. The author argues that this backlash is driven by the massive increase in the scale of facilities and a deep-seated public distrust of AI and 'Big Tech' companies.

item.title: Reading List 11/14/2026
item.description: This post provides a curated digest of diverse topics ranging from engineering failures and regulatory updates to hardware recycling and aviation safety. It serves as a collection of current events and technical updates relevant to the construction and technology sectors.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 14 November 2026
item.description: This weekly digest covers recent security updates and releases in package management, including critical patches for Composer, Podman, and pnpm. It also notes a change in GitHub policy regarding Dependabot alerts for inactive repositories.

item.title: The longest polynomial level set
item.description: This article discusses the mathematical problem of finding the polynomial with leading coefficient 1 that results in the longest level set curve defined by |p(z)| = 1 for a given degree. It highlights the recent proof by Teng Zhang, which confirms Erdős's long-standing conjecture that the polynomial p(z) = z^n - 1 yields this maximum length.

item.title: Peeking inside the bash rabbit hole
item.description: This article explores the utility of obscure Bash shell features as a productive way to take a break from more complex work. It highlights specific shortcuts, such as using the '!$' command to reference the last argument of a previous command.

item.title: Theatre Review: FrankenTacit ★★☆☆☆
item.description: This review evaluates 'FrankenTacit,' a unique theatrical performance by Seoul's Tacit Group that blends Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein with Korean algorave music. The show features a human performer collaborating with two AIs to create live-generated audio and visual experiences.

item.title: datasette-llm 0.1a11
item.description: The datasette-llm plugin has released version 0.1a11, adding support for OpenAI-compatible API endpoints. This allows users to integrate locally hosted models from tools like Ollama or LM Studio directly into Datasette applications.

item.title: datasette-vega 0.7
item.description: Simon Willison has released version 0.7 of the datasette-vega plugin, updating it for compatibility with the latest Datasette versions and Datasette Lite. The update includes cosmetic improvements and enables the plugin to function within the browser-based Datasette Lite environment.

item.title: Ops needs friction
item.description: Jeff Geerling reflects on recent large-scale IT outages to explore the unique mindset required for operations versus development. He argues that the operational perspective is distinct from project management, emphasizing the necessity of managing system friction.

item.title: How to find meaning in large tech companies
item.description: This article explores strategies for employees to find personal meaning and purpose within the complex environments of large technology corporations. It provides actionable advice on aligning individual values with professional responsibilities and navigating corporate structures to create impact.

item.title: This Week on The Analog Antiquarian
item.description: This entry explores the historical and mechanical intricacies of the early computer game Titus Andronicus. It provides an in-depth look at the development context and design philosophy behind this vintage title.

item.title: The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development
item.description: The article explores the rapid acceleration of artificial intelligence development, suggesting that the pace of progress is mirroring mathematical breakthroughs. The author argues that based on current trajectories, the arrival of superintelligence is likely to occur by 2030.

item.title: Kepler and the dwarf
item.description: The author verifies the orbital period of a newly discovered dwarf planet candidate using Kepler’s third law. By performing a back-of-the-envelope calculation, the author demonstrates how physical laws can be applied to evaluate astronomical claims.

item.title: Long permutations and long cycles
item.description: This article explores the mathematical properties of permutations, specifically how repeatedly rearranging a set of elements eventually leads back to the original sequence. It explains the concept of cycle decomposition, illustrating how different elements move within cycles of varying lengths.

item.title: How can I make it easier to use the helper class that lets me pass more than one parameter to co_await?
item.description: This post discusses methods to simplify the usage of a helper class in C++ for passing multiple parameters to co_await. The focus is on reducing boilerplate code by eliminating the need to explicitly type the helper class name.

item.title: Gadget Review: Thermal Master P3 Lite - and Linux Instructions ★★★★⯪
item.description: This post reviews the Thermal Master P3 Lite thermal camera, highlighting its macro lens capability for inspecting electronic components. It compares the new model against previous Thermal Master iterations to evaluate its performance and utility.

item.title: Pluralistic: I told you so (13 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques how antitrust laws have been weakened by shifts in legal interpretation, rendering monopolies nearly immune to challenge. He explains that policy effectiveness relies on the interplay between substance, scope, and administrability, illustrating how modern regulatory environments fail to address digital-era corporate power.

item.title: datasette-cluster-map 0.19
item.description: Datasette-cluster-map version 0.19 has been released, featuring compatibility with Datasette 1.0a42 and a dependency update for OpenStreetMap tile requests. The post highlights the plugin's utility through a power plant map visualization that demonstrates Datasette's newly redesigned facets.

item.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
item.description: Datasette-leaflet version 0.3 has been released to address compatibility issues with OpenStreetMap's tile server policy. The plugin now modifies the referrer policy for tile requests to comply with tile server requirements while protecting user privacy.

item.title: NYC’s venture capitalists need to love themselves
item.description: Anil Dash argues that NYC venture capitalists must stop seeking validation from Silicon Valley, which he characterizes as an entity hostile to New York's values. He contends that this lack of self-esteem harms the local tech ecosystem and advocates for a more confident, independent approach to building businesses in the city.

item.title: SSA from bytecode: imperative pearl
item.description: The article explains the process of converting stack-based bytecode from the CRuby YARV virtual machine into a high-level Static Single Assignment (SSA) intermediate representation. It details how the author simplifies this complex transformation by statically tracking stack inputs and outputs to map bytecode instructions to SSA values.

item.title: First Strike
item.description: The article discusses the geopolitical dangers of the US-China AI race, arguing that zero-sum competition may lead to catastrophic outcomes like a preemptive ASI first strike. The author proposes a more cooperative economic strategy focused on energy and compute, while expressing concern over rising tensions.

item.title: Technology as a Search Problem
item.description: This article explores the fundamental mechanisms behind technological progress and how new innovations emerge and evolve over time. It frames the development of technology as a complex search problem, seeking to understand the underlying patterns of discovery.

item.title: How can I pass more than one parameter to co_await?
item.description: The author explains that the co_await operator technically accepts only a single parameter. However, this parameter can be a complex object, allowing developers to effectively pass multiple values.

item.title: I didn’t write a program with emoji, but I did use a control character
item.description: The author shares a brief anecdote about utilizing a control character in a program rather than using emojis. This post is a short reflection on technical implementation details typical of the blog's content.

item.title: Book Review: This Is for Everyone - Tim Berners-Lee ★★★☆☆
item.description: This blog post offers a lukewarm review of 'This Is for Everyone,' a biography about Tim Berners-Lee. The reviewer finds the book lacking in substance, describing it as an unsatisfying mix of family anecdotes that fails to provide significant insight into the web's creator or history.

item.title: Pluralistic: Uber's labor crash (12 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This article examines the pattern of 'premature truths' told by tech leaders like Elon Musk and Uber, arguing that promises of futuristic transportation are often calculated lies. It highlights how these companies manipulate public perception regarding labor practices and autonomous technology to maintain corporate dominance.

item.title: So you want to buy AI for your company
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This article provides a satirical overview of the overwhelming landscape of AI models, detailing various benchmarks and subjective recommendations for enterprise and developer use. It highlights the confusing variety of model versions while advising on specific tools and workflows for programmers.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.37
item.description: Simon Willison updates the llm-gemini tool to version 0.37 following the launch of Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. The post analyzes the confusing pricing structure of the new Gemini 4 series, noting the lack of significant cost differentiation between the models.

item.title: Monads in Lean
item.description: This post explains how to implement monads in Lean 4 to handle computations that may fail, such as division by zero. It demonstrates how to replace tedious manual error checking with a cleaner abstraction for propagating Option values.

item.title: Ms. Bashkansky, Please Do Not Build The Torment Nexus
item.description: This post serves as a critical response to the rise of brain-computer interface technology, specifically targeting the push for AI-integrated telepathy. Through a fictionalized scenario of a user experiencing mental distress from a neural interface, the author argues against the development of technologies that prioritize technical capability over ethical and human safety.

item.title: Making a Website in 2026
item.description: The author reflects on Pete Millspaugh's experiment with AI-generated websites, highlighting the hidden complexity of AI-selected tech stacks. The piece questions whether AI tools prioritize unnecessary overhead and how non-technical users should navigate the trade-offs of these automated architectural decisions.

item.title: Possible Futures
item.description: This piece explores potential future scenarios and trajectories. It serves as a high-level conceptual framework for considering how different paths might unfold.

item.title: This Week in Source Control: 11 November 2026
item.description: This article highlights the latest developments in version control, specifically focusing on GitHub's new 'Rubicon' storage architecture. It details how GitHub uses Azure Blob Storage and the Ref-CAS service to scale repository performance, allowing for thousands of concurrent pushes per second.

item.title: Why Am I So Tired If AI Is Doing All the Work?
item.description: The article explores why AI-assisted work leads to fatigue rather than time savings. It argues that while AI makes initiating tasks easier, the burden of reviewing and verifying AI-generated output continues to consume significant human cognitive effort.

item.title: HowTo: Fix Eufy HomeBase 2 Storage Full Issues
item.description: This post provides a technical workaround for Eufy HomeBase 2 users experiencing storage capacity issues. It outlines a step-by-step process involving the use of an external USB memory stick and specific reformatting sequences to clear internal memory.

item.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
item.description: This article investigates the identity of the administrator behind the prominent ransomware group Qilin. By analyzing operational security mistakes made over the last decade, the author connects the group's activity to a 36-year-old individual residing in St. Petersburg, Russia.

item.title: Gemini Decisions API
item.description: Google has launched the Gemini Decisions API, a new model for handling yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring tasks. It distinguishes itself from competitors like OpenAI and Jev by offering full multi-modal support, including video, audio, and PDF processing.

item.title: aws-emulator
item.description: AWS has released an official emulator that allows developers to test their applications against local versions of AWS services without requiring paid API keys. Built using Rust, the project highlights the emerging trend of agentic engineering, having utilized massive AI-driven collaboration for its development.

item.title: Browse tools.simonwillison.net by tag
item.description: Simon Willison has updated his 'vibe-coded tools' collection by implementing a tag-based browsing system. He used tree-sitter to automatically analyze the code of over 200 tools, categorizing them by the JavaScript libraries and web APIs they utilize.

item.title: llm 0.37.2
item.description: Simon Willison has released LLM 0.37.2, which addresses two critical security vulnerabilities regarding the leakage of OpenAI API keys. The update ensures that keys are not accidentally sent to third-party providers when using the extra-openai-models configuration.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video
item.description: Anthropic's IPO roadshow video reveals their strategic focus on hardware-agnostic AI development, allowing them to train and deploy Claude across diverse chip architectures like NVIDIA, AMD, AWS, and Google. The company highlights their ability to rapidly port models to new hardware, such as AMD GPUs, using automated tools, which significantly enhances their total effective compute capacity.

item.title: We need more goat sacrifices
item.description: The article explores the history and philosophical implications of the O.J. Simpson trial, examining how it serves as a modern cultural touchstone for societal conflict. It critiques the obsession with truth and evidence in the face of deep-seated collective narratives.

item.title: Finally, Payment by Bank Transfer Comes to Have I Been Pwned
item.description: Troy Hunt announces that 'Have I Been Pwned' now supports bank transfers as a payment method. This update addresses long-standing friction in the service's payment process, making it more accessible for users.

item.title: I am searching for a coffee alternative
item.description: The author shares their experience of replacing coffee with caffeinated sparkling water after a positive trial with an office Bevi machine. Unable to replicate the experience at home, they conduct a taste test of various canned energy drinks against strict criteria regarding sugar and ingredients.

item.title: Revisiting Leander v Sweden and Big Brother Watch
item.description: This article examines the European Court of Human Rights jurisprudence, specifically Leander v Sweden and Big Brother Watch, in the context of modern cybersecurity and AI. It argues that previous legal standards for bulk surveillance may no longer be adequate given current technological advancements.

item.title: The classic console corner's CRT changeover
item.description: This post discusses the challenges of maintaining a setup for classic game consoles that require CRT displays to function correctly, particularly those using light guns. The author chronicles the history of their Panasonic Omnivision TV and explains why legacy hardware performs better on cathode-ray tube monitors than on modern flat panels.

item.title: Claude Code token cost explorer
item.description: The author shares a custom-built tool designed to analyze token usage within Claude Code, specifically addressing the difficulty of tracking costs when using subagents. The post provides a guide on using this local browser-based explorer to monitor and optimize LLM agent expenses.

item.title: Balanced Incomplete Block Designs
item.description: The article explains Balanced Incomplete Block Designs (BIBD) as a method for experimental design when resources are limited. It demonstrates how to effectively test multiple treatments, such as fertilizers, when dividing land into complete sets is impractical.

item.title: Microsoft employee price list from 1987
item.description: This post features a historical look at a 1987 price list for Microsoft products available to employees. It provides a nostalgic glimpse into the company's early pricing and software catalog.

item.title: Book Review: The Unfinished Harauld Hughes - Richard Ayoade ★★★⯪☆
item.description: The author revisits Richard Ayoade's latest book, comparing its abstract, genre-defying style to his earlier work. The review highlights the book's comedic but unconventional structure, noting it functions more as an 'anti-novel' than a traditional narrative.

item.title: Pluralistic: The EU should go big and hard over border IT failure (10 Nov 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow argues that the EU's legitimacy as a technocratic project depends on its ability to demonstrate tangible administrative competence. He critiques the reliance on massive, neoliberal public-private partnerships, suggesting these 'megaprojects' often fail and undermine public trust in government efficacy.

item.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
item.description: Microsoft released security updates addressing nearly 1,100 vulnerabilities, including 63 critical flaws such as a zero-day in Outlook. The update coincides with similar security releases from major tech companies like Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla.

item.title: llm-gemini 0.36
item.description: Simon Willison announces the release of llm-gemini 0.36, providing support for Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon model. The post outlines the model's pricing structure and demonstrates its capabilities through image generation and coding tasks.

item.title: Introducing Our Smallest, Most Efficient Model: Muse Ember
item.description: Meta AI has released Muse Ember, a new efficient model optimized for agentic workflows like coding and tool use. This summary compares its pricing and token limits against competitors like GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku.

item.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
item.description: Anthropic's documentation for Claude Fable 5.2 reveals that explicitly stating ownership of a codebase in prompts significantly improves the model's ability to optimize structure. Using a specific framing instruction helps the model avoid redundant code by treating the project as its own responsibility.

item.title: Yonkers Rises
item.description: Simon Willison demonstrates the generative 3D modeling and animation capabilities of Claude Fable 5.2. By prompting the AI to turn the city of Yonkers into a mech that traverses New York, he showcases how models can interpret complex natural language instructions and typos to create Three.js animations.

item.title: Glue work is still harmful in the age of AI
item.description: This article argues that 'glue work'—the unglamorous, often invisible tasks required to keep projects moving—remains detrimental to professional growth even with the integration of AI. It suggests that AI tools do not eliminate the burden of coordination and maintenance, but rather may shift how these essential tasks impact an engineer's career trajectory.

item.title: Weekly Update 529: Kids Social Media Bans (and Everything Else)
item.description: Troy Hunt critiques the legislative approach to banning social media for children, arguing that policymakers fail to identify where the responsibility for enforcement truly resides. The post highlights the inadequacies of the current political discourse surrounding these age-restriction laws.

item.title: Addition By Subtraction
item.description: The author argues for the power of simplification by removing unnecessary features from their icon gallery website. By reducing the number of size options from four to three, they successfully minimized cognitive overhead for users while maintaining core functionality.

item.title: Yak-Shaving Overload
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: The author reflects on the pitfalls of 'yak-shaving'—the tendency for tech projects to spiral into endless, complex side tasks—while attempting to revitalize an abandoned JingPad Linux tablet using AI tools. The piece highlights how relying too heavily on AI to solve technical roadblocks can lead to frustrating, unproductive rabbit holes.
